science.title: October's moon phases offer something for astronomers and casual skywatchers alike
science.description: October's night sky will feature two notable lunar events, giving both seasoned astronomers and casual observers a reason to spend some time looking up. The month includes a new moon on Oct. 10 and the Hunter's Moon later in October, offering dramatically different viewing experiences depending on what people hope to see in the night sky. Abigail Sadowski, a resident astronomer with the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada's Kalium Observatory in Regina, said the new moon period is especially valuable for people hoping to observe objects beyond the Moon itself. New moon creates darker skies A new moon occurs when the Moon is positioned roughly between Earth and the Sun.
